title: "God Led Me to Hewlett": The Auditor and the Regulator Behind Allen Stanford

lines.say: Every year, Allen Stanford's bank published audited reports. The auditor was a one-man firm in Antigua, C.A.S. Hewlett.
In sixteen years, prosecutors said, he never got the documents to verify the assets. He signed off anyway.
lines.show: In 16 years, prosecutors said, he never got the documents to verify the assets. He signed off anyway.

lines.say: Prosecutors said Stanford paid him more than three point three million dollars from a Swiss account. According to his finance chief, Stanford told him: God led me to Hewlett.
lines.show: Prosecutors said Stanford paid him more than $3.3 million from a Swiss account. According to his finance chief, Stanford told him: "God led me to Hewlett."

lines.say: The regulator was Leroy King, head of Antigua's financial watchdog. He admitted taking about five hundred twenty-one thousand dollars in cash from Stanford.
lines.show: The regulator was Leroy King, head of Antigua's financial watchdog. He admitted taking about $521,000 in cash from Stanford.

scene.label: cash from Stanford,|by his own admission

lines.say: When the S.E.C. sent King a confidential request in two thousand five, prosecutors said he passed it straight to Stanford.
lines.show: When the SEC sent King a confidential request in 2005, prosecutors said he passed it straight to Stanford.

lines.say: King was sentenced to ten years. Stanford, to one hundred ten.
lines.show: King was sentenced to ten years. Stanford, to 110.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
